title: The Race to the Top
objective: After this level you can explain the race to build the tallest building.
summary: The Chrysler Building won 1929's race with a secret spire; the CTBUH counts spires, not antennas, which let the Petronas Towers pass the Sears Tower in 1998. The title moved from New York to Dubai.

cards.headline: On October 23, 1929, a secret spire rose out of the Chrysler Building.
cards.body: It had been assembled inside the building's crown in five sections. Then it was hoisted into place in about 90 minutes. The Chrysler Building was racing another tower for the title of the world's tallest, and this was the winning move.

cards.headline: The rival downtown
cards.body: The rival was 40 Wall Street, rising at the same time downtown. The Chrysler's architect, William Van Alen, kept his trump card hidden until the last moment, and the finished tower stood 1,046 feet tall. The victory didn't last. Built between 1928 and 1930, it held the record only until the Empire State Building opened in 1931.

cards.headline: What counts as the top?
cards.body: A race needs rules. In 1998 the Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur took the title from Chicago's Sears Tower, even though the Sears roof was more than 200 feet higher. The Petronas spires were counted as part of the architecture. Today the CTBUH measures to a building's architectural top: spires count, antennas don't.

mascot.line: Moral of the story: if you're racing, wear a pointy hat, not an antenna.

cards.headline: The title moves around the world

events.label: New York: the Chrysler Building, with its secret spire
New York: the Empire State Building, tallest until 1970
Chicago: the Sears Tower passes New York's World Trade Center
Kuala Lumpur: the Petronas Towers, spires and all
Dubai: Burj Khalifa, 828 meters, tallest as of 2026
